messages:

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated pool + burst needs (Arcadia)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are preparing our capacity ask for the pilot and want to lock down how Redwood will handle burst traffic. A few items we need clarity on: 1) max sustained RPS per GPU you recommend for our Llama-2-13B workload, 2) how burst credits are allocated for reserved customers, and 3) what automatic autoscale thresholds would look like (latency SLOs vs cost trade-offs).

Attached is our RFP that includes traffic profiles (peaks during batch scoring windows). Can you propose an operational policy we can include in the pilot contract? Procurement will need the exact failure modes and rollback behavior for the Dedicated pool.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Tom Wu
VP Engineering, Arcadia Labs
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated pool + burst needs (Arcadia)

Tom —

Thanks for the RFP (got it). I pulled together a concise runbook and a proposed burst/autoscale framework tailored to your traffic patterns. High level summary up front: 1) Baseline reserve: 8 GPUs dedicated (A100-class equivalent) to meet your 95th percentile throughput; 2) Shoulder buffer: automatic soft-burst up to +30% capacity using ephemeral preemptible slots; 3) Credit-backed hard burst: additional pooled capacity up to +80% for short windows (credit consumption rate documented); 4) Autoscale triggers: a combination of 99th-percentile latency breach over a 60s rolling window OR sustained queue depth above threshold for 120s.

I attached two files: redwood_burst_matrix.xlsx (policy matrix + credit math) and a draft runbook. If acceptable we can bake this into the pilot SOW with explicit eviction and rollback sequences.

Would you like us to walk procurement through the failure scenarios? Happy to schedule a short call.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Arcadia — burst policy one-pager + SOW failure-mode snippet

Hi Samantha and team —

Quick reply with the one-pager and failure-mode language inline below. Summary bullets for SOW insertion: 

- Typical burst duration: shoulder buffer (ephemeral preemptible) is designed for short transients (median 45s, 90th percentile < 4 minutes) driven by queueing smoothing; hard burst credits can sustain larger dips in capacity for longer windows (typical safe window ~ 10 minutes at +80% depending on cluster-wide contention).
- Preemption behavior: ephemeral slots are best-effort and subject to earlier eviction to satisfy higher-priority reserved capacity; when preemption occurs requests are automatically routed to remaining dedicated GPUs or to pinned model fallbacks.
- SLA carve-outs: burst capacity is provided as best-effort; latency SLOs for dedicated baseline are contract-backed. During credit-backed hard bursts, latency SLO degradation is expected and will not count as SLA violations if documented credit consumption was in effect.
- Rollback and safe-fallthrough: automatic model variant fallback (quantized variant) will be enabled if tail latency exceeds threshold for >120s; customers receive telemetry and an automated incident stub.

Attached: arcadia_capacity_RFP.pdf (we received your RFP) and the redwood_burst_matrix.xlsx that breaks down credit math and cost uplift.

If this wording looks good we can provide a concise clause for your SOW and a slide that procurement can review. Proposed next step: 30-min procurement walk-through on Friday 09:00 PT.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
